A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUARDIAN study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, API-call counts, anomaly-detection results, parameter analyses, and multi-agent case studies in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds false-discovery-rate, sparse-topology, and runtime evaluations in Tables 2, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: The graph representation, GCN/Transformer encoders, dual reconstruction decoders, information-bottleneck objective, incremental training, and pruning procedure are retained. Added explanations and the corrected hyperparameter derivation in Appendix A.10 do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: The four datasets and three safety scenarios remain. v2 adds a limited network-environment extension: MATH evaluation with sparse communication graphs, connecting agents to 25%, 50%, or 75% of agents in subsequent rounds (Table 3).

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same baselines: LLM Debate, DyLAN, SelfCheckGPT, Challenger, and Inspector, with scenario-specific membership unchanged. The new sparsity and runtime comparisons reuse existing methods; no new comparator is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds FDR measurement, average runtime per question under communication-targeted attacks, and specified connectivity levels for the new topology tests. Existing sampling, backbone models, default agent count, and attack timing remain unchanged. Separate per-dataset training is newly documented, rather than established as a changed setting.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends diagnostic coverage with false-removal analysis and sparse-topology robustness tests, addressing intervention reliability and behavior beyond fully connected networks. Appendix Figures 10 and 12 also revise qualitative case evidence. Existing parameter sensitivity and agent-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent testing iterations. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing. FDR is introduced as a detection-performance metric, not an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Retained quantitative tables preserve their values, but v2 adds substantial results on new evaluation axes: FDR ranges from 8.32% to 30.67%; GUARDIAN achieves 52.2%, 56.1%, and 57.3% accuracy at the three connectivity levels; and runtime measurements include 45.19 seconds on MATH versus LLM Debate's 40.31 seconds. Figure 10 changes from two-round consensus after one removal to three-round consensus after two removals, while Figure 12 revises agent responses. These are added or revised findings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.10 corrects the derivation from gamma = lambda/(1 + beta) to gamma = lambda/(1 + lambda beta), explicitly deriving and normalizing the reconstruction coefficient. Definition 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and the Appendix A.2 proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces general pioneering language with an explicit claim to the first systematic application of information-bottleneck principles to safety in LLM multi-agent collaboration. The principal claims about model-agnostic defense, accuracy, and efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits the evaluated learning setting to separate per-dataset models and in-distribution episodes. It adds explanations attributing tolerance of false removals to redundancy and one-agent-per-round pruning, topology robustness to structural reconstruction, and runtime savings to reduced calls and waiting.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer in the abstract and newly documents separate per-dataset training. Section 3.2 clarifies that agents access only directly connected predecessors from the immediately preceding round. These are access and implementation disclosures, without evidence of changed underlying procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Face3DAdv, Reinforced Embodied Active Defense, and MLA-Trust, and makes the information-bottleneck priority claim more explicit. The related-work discussion and overall positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical corrections, expands method and evaluation explanations, rewrites Appendix A.10, and converts the two numbered related-work subsections into run-in headings. The overall section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the experimental displays with three new tables and revises appendix case-study figures, notably adding another detection stage and discussion round to Figure 10. Several diagrams are enlarged, retained tables and plots are repositioned or resized, and colored cross-references are introduced.

improvement.justification: The new FDR, topology, and runtime evaluations provide useful checks missing from v1, while Appendix A.10 fixes an algebraic error and the code pointer improves access information. The gains remain bounded: the added tests mainly use GPT-3.5-turbo, and the claim that false removals cause minimal downstream harm lacks a separately quantified degradation analysis. The revision improves validation and transparency without resolving these limitations.
